title: Trapping Rain Water II
description:
Given an `m x n` integer matrix `heightMap` representing the height of each unit cell in a 2D elevation map, return the total volume of water it can trap after raining.

Water can flow out of a cell into any of its four orthogonally adjacent neighbors (up, down, left, right) and drains off the outer edges of the grid. A cell `(r, c)` holds water up to the minimum possible maximum elevation along any path from `(r, c)` to the boundary of the matrix.
hints: Water cannot be trapped on the outer boundary of the grid. Think of the boundary as a shrinking dam enclosing the unvisited interior.
Put all boundary cells into a min-heap ordered by effective water level `(height, r, c)` and mark them visited.

Repeatedly pop the lowest boundary cell `(h, r, c)`. Any unvisited neighbor `(nr, nc)` traps `max(0, h - heightMap[nr][nc])` water and enters the heap with effective wall height `max(h, heightMap[nr][nc])`.

examples.explanation: Interior cells at row 1 fill to water level 3: (1,1) traps 1 unit, (1,2) traps 2 units, and (1,4) traps 1 unit, for a total of 4.
Surrounded by a height-3 rim, the eight height-2 interior cells each trap 1 unit and the central height-1 cell traps 2 units, totaling 10 units.
Every cell in a 2x2 grid is on the outer boundary, so no water can be trapped.
